name: Hess’s seafloor-spreading proposal
description: Hess proposed that new ocean floor forms near ridges and moves away, giving a possible mechanism relevant to continental movement.

date.basis: Year is the date of the described episode in the cited source, not necessarily the invention or first conception.

events.statement: Hess formally proposed a concept later known as seafloor spreading.

evidence.locator: Discussion of Hess and seafloor spreading
evidence.supports: Identifies Hess’s formal 1962 proposal and describes its relevance to continental drift.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established from the sources collected for this scoped record, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The proposal developed in a broader research community and preceded the later integrated theory of plate tectonics; this episode is not a claim that Hess supplied all supporting evidence.

research.note: Independent second reading checked the dated event evidence; other facets remain as previously assessed.
